title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — after the law innate vice flared; Adam-act imputation stayed hidden
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: once the law was given, innate vice showed itself far more clearly and overflowed with worst fruits. But imputation of Adam’s first actual sin stayed as hidden as before—no precept, threat, or sentence declared it. Indeed that imputation cannot stand with Moses’ law (he will show later). So Paul would have used ‘until the law’ in vain if the question were one man’s actual sin imputed to all.
pass_b_english: When the law was given, innate vice showed itself far more clearly than before, and overflowed with a wealth of the worst fruits.
But the imputation of the first actual sin stayed as hidden as before, declared by no precept of the law, by no threat, by no sentence.
Indeed that imputation cannot stand with the Mosaic law, as, God favoring, I will make plain in its place.
In vain, therefore, would the Apostle have used that circumscription of time, until the law, if the question had been about that sort of one man’s actual sin imputed to all.
source_text: Lata lege vitium innatum sese multo quam antea clarius prodidit, ac pessimorum fructuum copia redundavit. Sed imputatio primi peccati actualis tam latuit quam antea, nullo legis praecepto, nulla comminatione, nulla sententia declarata. Immo illa imputatio cum lege Mosaica stare non potest, ut, Deo bene favente, suo loco planum faciam. Frustra igitur Apostolus illam temporis circumscriptionem adhibuisset usque ad legem, si de eiusmodi peccato actuali unius hominis omnibus imputato quaestio fuisset.

choices.choice: Law made vice clear; Adam-act imputation stayed undeclared
